requirement: EPIC-1 · Story 1.4 — 32-step grid visualizer synced to the pad and click. A 32-step grid (2 bars × 16, 16th-note resolution) shows the current pattern with lane rows (drums as kick/snare/hat lanes + a bass note lane) and a playhead that sweeps across the 32 cells in time with the metronome click. The playhead position is driven by Tone.Transport time (via Tone.Draw), never a separate timer, so it never drifts from the click over a long loop. Tapping a grid cell toggles/sets a hit (and plays the mapped ROK sound) — this is the shared edit surface that story 3.1 (grid editor) extends. A hit placed on the pad appears on the grid and vice versa: while playing with REC engaged, pad taps are quantized to the current step and written into the pattern; grid edits play the same sound a pad tap would. ALL timing goes through Tone.Transport / Tone.Draw — no setInterval, no custom clock.

architecture.decision: No new design fork — the pattern data model is dictated by the already-locked Lesson JSON schema (README): layers with drums hits [{step, sound}] and bass notes [{step, pad, octave, length}], step 0-31. Story 1.4 introduces a minimal in-memory Pattern store shaped so it maps 1:1 onto those schema layers; stories 3.1 (grid editor) and 3.2 (persistence/export) extend and serialize it. Playhead sync uses Tone.Transport + Tone.Draw, consistent with the story-1.3 lock (no setInterval).
seams: src/pattern.ts owns the live Pattern type + pure helpers. Pattern shape ergonomic for toggling AND trivially convertible to Lesson-schema layers: { drums: { kick: boolean[32]; snare: boolean[32]; hat: boolean[32] }; bass: (BassCell | null)[32] } where BassCell = { pad: PadId; octave: number; length: number }. Helpers: emptyPattern(), toggleDrum(pattern, sound, step), setBass(pattern, step, cell)/clearBass(pattern, step). This is the load-bearing store 3.1/3.2 build on — do NOT collapse it to a shape that loses per-step drum sound or bass pitch/octave.

src/transport.ts gains onStep(cb: (step: number) => void): () => void firing the current 16th-note step index 0..31 once per 16th note, scheduled via Tone.Transport.scheduleRepeat('16n') and dispatched inside Tone.Draw.schedule (paint-synced, sample-accurate). It coexists with the existing onBeat (0..7) — both reset to 0 on startTransport and are driven by the same Transport, so they stay coherent. This is the ONLY playhead source; the grid must not run its own timer.

src/StepGrid.tsx renders 4 lane rows (kick, snare, hat, bass) × 32 cells from the Pattern, highlights the playhead column via an onStep subscription, and calls back on cell click to toggle a hit. App owns the Pattern state (useState) and the current-step, passes them down, and plays the mapped ROK sound (audio.ts playPad / players) on both grid-cell edits and captured pad taps.

Pad->grid capture (bidirectional): while isPlaying() && recording, App writes a pad tap into the Pattern at the current step — drum mode via padDrum(padId) into that drum lane, bass mode as a BassCell at that step. Free play (not recording) still just sounds. Grid->pad direction = a grid cell edit plays the same sound path a pad tap uses.

tasks.title: Pad->grid REC capture (bidirectional) + full sync/no-drift browser verification
tasks.intent: Make the pad and grid a single shared surface. In src/App.tsx, extend handlePad so that when isPlaying() && recording, the pad tap is captured into the Pattern at the CURRENT step (the latest step from the onStep subscription — App must track current step in state from onStep, or read it): drums mode writes into the padDrum(padId) lane via toggleDrum/setDrum-on at that step; bass mode writes a BassCell { pad: padId, octave: 0, length: 1 } at that step via setBass. Free play (not recording, or stopped) keeps only sounding — no capture. The captured hit must appear in the grid immediately (same pattern state the grid renders). Keep quantization simple: capture at the current 16th-note step (the playhead position). Add a ponytail: comment noting capture quantizes to the current step and richer editing lives in 3.1. Do not regress grid-cell editing, playhead sync, or any 1.1-1.3 behavior.
